Either sighting disproves the conjunction. The supporting measurements live in attempt.MC_writegauntletsave-addic-fusion-five-axes.20260901.v1 (probe W3 flipped cmplwi to cmpwi by retyping alone and did NOT produce addic.) and attempt.MC_loadgauntletsave-d3-hoist-blockers-closed.20260901.v3 (the retained volatile baseline DOES produce addic. because the qualifier forbids the hoist). subject: tu:game/sys/memcard
value:
MWCC GC 1.2.5 family. TELL: the target has `addic. rD,rS,-K` feeding both an `mtctr` and a `beq` zero-trip guard, and OUR build has a plain `addi` somewhere far upstream plus a separate `cmpwi`/`cmplwi` at the loop. TWO independent conditions must BOTH hold before the fusion forms, and probing them one at a time reads as a dead axis when only one is missing.

CONDITION 1 - THE COUNTER MUST BE SIGNED. `addic.` records a SIGNED comparison into CR0. A counter declared `u32` forces the front end to spell the `!= 0` test as the unsigned `cmplwi`, which MWCC will not fuse with a signed-recording arithmetic instruction. MEASURED, writeGauntletSave (game/sys/memcard): retyping `u32 count;` to `s32 count;` with no other edit moved the multiset from `ours-only -1 cmplwi` to `ours-only -1 cmpwi` - the compare became signed - while real, instruction count and every cluster stayed exactly where they were (149, T190/O191). A pure spelling win with zero score movement, which is precisely how a NECESSARY-BUT-INSUFFICIENT condition presents.

CONDITION 2 - THE SUBTRACTION MUST STILL BE AT THE TEST. If the loop bound is `bigLocal - K` where bigLocal holds a single constant assigned outside the loop, MWCC folds the subtraction INTO the constant's materialization far upstream and parks the result in a callee-saved register, leaving only a compare at the loop. The fusion then has nothing to fuse. MEASURED in writeGauntletSave: the target emits `lis r31,1` alone at 0x9c and computes `addic. r6,r31,-23992` at the loop at 0x1b4, while ours emits `lis r6,1` at 0x90 AND `addi r25,r6,-23992` at 0xa0, then `cmpwi r25,0` at 0x1b8. That surplus `addi` is the function's entire instruction-count delta (191 vs target 190).

HOW TO DEFEAT CONDITION 2 - and, more usefully, HOW NOT TO. `volatile` on the operand DOES forbid the hoist and DOES restore the fusion: it is why loadGauntletSave's retained baseline (real 628, `volatile bigSize`) gets `addic. r0,r4,-23992` right at 0x940 while every de-volatile probe loses it. But volatile is only correct when the TARGET reloads the operand from memory at the loop. In loadGauntletSave the target does `lwz r4,180(r1)` immediately before the addic., so volatile matches. In writeGauntletSave the target holds the operand in register r31 and never reloads it, so volatile would ADD a load the target does not have and move away from the answer. CHECK WHETHER THE TARGET RELOADS BEFORE REACHING FOR THE QUALIFIER.

MEASURED-DEAD ways to defeat condition 2, four distinct forms, none of which worked on either function: moving the subtraction into the for-init (neutral-IDENTICAL, object bytes unchanged - statement position never reaches codegen); sinking the operand's definition below the loop-back label (neutral on both functions); block-scoping the counter to split its web (neutral); and a scoped `#pragma opt_lifetimes off` (regressed 754 -> 944 and the hoist SURVIVED, proving the hoist is not lifetime/LICM-class and that opt_lifetimes is the wrong instrument - do not respell it).

PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE. When a residual needs a conjunction, the standard three-probes-per-axis budget silently misprices it: each condition alone measures NEUTRAL, so an agent probing them separately collects two neutrals and correctly concludes 'axis dead' about a mechanism that is one joint probe from closing. This is the same failure mode AGENTS.md discipline 6 records for two-variable axes, arriving here through codegen conditions rather than through two source edits. Any next probe on this class must satisfy BOTH conditions in ONE edit.
